Jordan: quick heads-up — local perf runs show the kernel pick flips for some cards when seq_len > 2048, causing ~12% p99 regression. repro + traces attached.
Maya: which kernel path is flipping?
Jordan: runtime currently picks fast_attn_v2 for sm86 when tc available, but on a subset of our fleet it falls back to generic_matmul at ~seq_len 2100. detection looks like sm=86, tc reported, but kernel probe returns incompatible, so we end up on fallback.
Ken: do we have device signature diffs? driver version / pci ids? could be a driver quirk.
Pranav: ran a quick microbench across three boxes:
```
# device,driver,seq_len,kernel,tokens_sec,p99_ms
sm86,537.21,1024,fast_attn_v2,120000,18
sm86,537.21,2048,fast_attn_v2,110000,22
sm86,540.11,2112,generic_matmul,96000,34
sm75,515.48,2112,generic_matmul,72000,45
```
Jordan: see the drop at 2112 where kernel flips and p99 spikes.
perf-bot: nvprof summary (attached): kernel generic_matmul shows much higher shared memory bank conflicts and lower tensor core utilization on the impacted nodes; L2 miss rate up ~8%. Also observed KV cache eviction bump correlating with batch splits.
Lina: that smells like KV prefetch + batch splitting boundary. if the request bundler splits into microbatches for >2048 we may evict prefixes and then cause mem churn.
Maya: agreed. Could be two separate problems: 1) capability detection returning inconsistent tensor-core availability on driver 540.x and 2) seqlen gating threshold that forces batch-splitting heuristics to different code paths.
Ken: suggestion: add a soft-hysteresis around seq_len boundary and a device-cap override flag so we can force tensor-core path for canary hosts. also add logging: hw_sig + kernel_choice at boot probe.
Pranav: +1 for device override. I put up a tiny patch that exposes REDWOOD_FORCE_TC=1 to the runtime; tested on one node and it keeps fast_attn_v2 alive past 2200 seq_len, tokens/sec back to expected and p99 down ~10ms.
Jordan: nice. we should be careful though — if TC actually misbehaves we'll get correctness or small perf regressions. need unit microbench + correctness fuzz.
Maya: can we gate the override behind a perf-check that runs a short microbench on startup? if kernel shows >80% tc_util and verifies output within tolerance, flip it on.
Lina: also let's add KV cache instrumentation: per-route prefix evictions, life/window, and the batch-split event id. current logs are too sparse to attribute thrash.
Ken: I'll open an action item: add hw_sig -> kernel_probe mapping to the onboarding table and a smoke microbench that validates tc path. assign to eng-runtime infra.
Pranav: filing canary rollout plan: 1) enable REDWOOD_FORCE_TC on 5 canary GPUs 2) collect perf and correctness for 24h 3) if stable, roll heuristics change to add +10% seqlen hysteresis and new KV prefetch guard.
Jordan: thanks — can someone paste the minimal repro command we used?
Pranav: `./rbench --model=gpt2-xl --batch=8 --seq=2112 --device=sm86 --kernels=probe`
perf-bot: note: also saw driver 540.11 report tc_capable=true but tensorcore_launch failed with error 7 on one host. might be a runtime API quirk.
Maya: ok plan of record: Ken add probe/logs + smoke bench (today), Pranav run canary rollout (tomorrow), Lina add KV instrumentation (T+2 days). I'll pair with Jordan to draft a brief postmortem if canary shows variance. :thinking:
Jordan: thanks team — let's keep thread updates here. :thumbsup:
